name: create_qp_common
prose: Precondition: dev, pd, init_attr and caller_qp are valid; *caller_qp is NULL (the function allocates the QP) or a preallocated QP; for a user PD udata holds the create-QP command. It first classifies the QP type; a tunnel QP request whose proxy type is not SMI or GSI, or made on a non-master device, returns -EINVAL. If *caller_qp is NULL it allocates an sqp or qp structure (-ENOMEM on failure, returning at once). It sets up the RQ size (set_rq_size); then for a user PD copies the create command (-EFAULT on failure), sets the SQ size, pins the buffer with ib_umem_get (PTR_ERR on failure), and initialises and writes the MTT; for a kernel PD it handles the NETIF flag (if IB_QP_CREATE_NETIF_QP is requested but device-managed steering is not supported it jumps to the err label with err still 0, i.e. it returns 0 without creating a QP, freeing a QP allocated here), sets the kernel SQ size, allocates the doorbell, the QP buffer (with a smaller-alignment retry) and the MTT, and the sq/rq wrid arrays (-ENOMEM on failure). For a special QP number (sqpn) of proxy SMI, SMI owner or GSI type it allocates proxy buffers with alloc_proxy_bufs (-ENOMEM on failure); otherwise it reserves a QP number (steering-managed for NETIF). It then calls mlx4_qp_alloc, sets the doorbell QPN, sets *caller_qp if it was NULL, and under the reset-flow resource lock adds the QP to the device list and the send and receive CQ lists, and returns 0. Failures after the buffers exist unwind through labels: err_qpn releases the reserved QPN when sqpn is 0; err_proxy frees proxy buffers only when the QP type is MLX4_IB_QPT_PROXY_GSI (proxy SMI and SMI owner buffers allocated at 841 are not freed on these paths); then the doorbell mapping or wrid arrays, the MTT, the buffer or umem, and the doorbell are released as applicable; at err a QP allocated by this call (*caller_qp NULL) is freed. The function returns the saved negative errno (or 0 on success or the NETIF-unsupported path).
note: Round 15 and round 17 reviewers are right: proxy buffers are allocated for PROXY_SMI_OWNER, PROXY_SMI and PROXY_GSI (mlx4_ib_qp.c:838-845) but err_proxy frees them only for PROXY_GSI (913-915), so the old claim that every resource is released was wrong. The NETIF-unsupported return of 0 (775-781) was already stated. Real function at 642-942 (slice 759-1024 cut the head). Read in full except a few lines; helper functions not read. The portion between 876-904 (qp registration) was read once.

name: try_add_to_existing_fg
prose: Precondition: ft is a flow table, match_head lists the candidate flow groups, ft_version is the table version snapshot taken before the search; the caller holds the node references the mlx5 flow-steering code expects. It allocates a scratch fte with alloc_fte; if that fails it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) (whatever alloc_fte's error was). Unless FLOW_ACT_NO_APPEND is set it first searches the groups for an existing fte matching the spec: if one is found (lookup_fte_locked) it calls add_rule_fg on it, releases the found fte's lock and reference, frees the scratch fte and returns add_rule_fg's result, which can be a rule or an ERR_PTR. If no existing fte is used, it returns ERR_PTR(-EAGAIN) (freeing the scratch fte) when the table version has changed; if the group list version changed since the search it retries the search with write locking. Then for each active group it tries insert_fte(g, fte): on -ENOSPC it goes on to the next group; on any other error it frees the scratch fte and returns ERR_PTR(err); on success it calls add_rule_fg on the inserted fte (the scratch fte now being the inserted one and not freed) and returns that result, and if add_rule_fg returned an error it also drops the inserted fte with tree_put_node. If no group accepted the fte it frees the scratch fte and returns ERR_PTR(-ENOENT).
note: Both reviewers right: on add_rule_fg failure after insert_fte the inserted fte is released with tree_put_node, not freed (mlx5_fs_core.c:1941-1945), and add_rule_fg's error is returned. Real function at 1853-1951 (slice 1792-2044). Read in full; helper functions not read. The retry condition at 1914-1917 and the active-group test at 1925 are described as coded.

name: init_one
prose: Precondition: pdev is a PCI device being probed by this driver and id is NULL or the matching pci_device_id. It allocates the softc with kzalloc_node and does not check the result for failure before using it. It stores the NUMA node and pci_dev_data, falls back to the default profile if mlx5_prof_sel is out of range, sets the device description, initialises the sysctl context and adds several scalar sysctls (return values ignored), then creates the pme_stats, pme_stats errors and caps (with current and max subnodes) sysctl nodes; if any of those node creations returns NULL it sets err = -ENOMEM and jumps to clean_sysctl_ctx (which frees the sysctl context and the softc). The opaque capability sysctls (SYSCTL_ADD_OPAQUE) and the counters are added without checking for failure. It then initialises lists, locks and the dump_lock, and calls mlx5_pci_init, mlx5_health_init, mlx5_pagealloc_init, mlx5_fs_core_alloc and mlx5_load_one in order; a nonzero error from mlx5_pci_init, mlx5_health_init, mlx5_fs_core_alloc or mlx5_load_one is logged and the matching cleanup labels run in reverse (flow steering freed, page allocator and health cleaned up, PCI closed, dump lock destroyed, sysctl context freed, softc freed with kfree) and the error is returned. On success it calls mlx5_fwdump_prep and mlx5_firmware_update (results not used); under PCI_IOV, when the vport group manager capability is set it reads the SR-IOV VF total, calls mlx5_eswitch_init, and only if that succeeds sets up the IOV schemas and calls pci_iov_attach; dev->iov_pf is set true only if pci_iov_attach also succeeds, and failures of either are only logged. It then calls pci_save_state and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: failures of the SYSCTL_ADD_OPAQUE and counter additions are not checked (mlx5_main.c:1519-1674), so 'capability nodes created' is true only for the node containers and not for each leaf. Real function at 1404-1769 (slice 1571-1823 cut the head). Read in full (a long repetitive sysctl block was only skimmed); callee functions not read.

name: mlx5e_create_ethtool
prose: Precondition: priv is an initialised mlx5e_priv whose mdev, params and sysctl_ctx are set up; the function returns nothing and takes no locks. It fills priv->params_ethtool from priv->params and the device capabilities, and, when the disable_local_lb_mc or disable_local_lb_uc capability is set, queries the multicast and unicast local loopback state (a failed query leaves that field unchanged). It then creates the "conf" sysctl node and returns immediately if that returns NULL; otherwise it registers one read-only or read-write handler per entry of mlx5e_params_desc (read-only for names containing _max or _mtu). It creates the "fec" node and returns immediately if that is NULL; if mlx5e_fec_update returns 0 it registers the FEC mode and mask sysctls. It registers debug_stats and the PCI device-name string, calls mlx5e_create_diagnostics, and creates the "qos" node, returning immediately if that returns NULL. Under qos it registers tc_max_rate only when mlx5e_getmaxrate returns 0, tc_rate_share only when mlx5e_get_max_alloc returns 0, prio_0_7_tc only when mlx5e_get_prio_tc returns 0, and, when mlx5e_get_dscp returns 0, the dscp_%d_%d_prio sysctls for i = 0, 8, ... below MLX5_MAX_SUPPORTED_DSCP and trust_state; it registers buffers_size, buffers_prio and cable_length only when mlx5e_port_query_buffer returns 0, and hw_temperature when mlx5e_hw_temperature_update returns 0. The results of the individual SYSCTL_ADD_* calls other than the three node creations are not checked, and the registered entries belong to priv->sysctl_ctx.
note: Packet name mlx5e_create_qos_sysctls does not exist; the slice 1547-1637 is the tail of mlx5e_create_ethtool at mlx5_en_ethtool.c:1419-1637 (read in full, sysctl option lines skimmed), so it is fixed under that name. The old prose covered only the tail and said the hw_temperature node goes under priv->sysctl_ifnet, which is not shown in the portion read (not verified); it is not claimed now. Reviewer reasons were only mechanical.

name: mlx5e_sq_tls_xmit
prose: Precondition: sq, parg and *ppmb are valid and the mbuf has a packet header. It returns MLX5E_TLS_CONTINUE without touching parg if the mbuf has no CSUM_SND_TAG flag or its send tag type is not TLS (or TLS rate-limit when RATELIMIT is built). It computes the full header size and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE if the size is 0 or no TCP header is found. If the whole packet is just headers, or mlx5e_sq_tls_populate returns 0 (no TLS record header could be filled in), it sets parg->tisn to 0 and parg->ihs to the header size and returns MLX5E_TLS_CONTINUE. Otherwise it takes the tag lock only around a state check: an INIT tag releases the lock and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE; a SETUP tag becomes TXRDY with expected_seq forced to a value different from the packet sequence; the lock is released in every case before continuing. If expected_seq differs from the TCP sequence number of the packet (out of order) it calls sbtls_recover_record: a NULL result counts a tx error and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE; otherwise, when the recovered data starts a record it sets the initial record number, sends the static and progress parameter work requests and, if the recovered mbuf carries no data, sends a NOP, sets expected_seq to the packet sequence and returns MLX5E_TLS_LOOP. In the other out-of-order cases it sets parg->tisn and parg->mst and sends the recovered data with mlx5e_sq_dump_xmit: on failure it frees the recovered mbuf, sets expected_seq to the recovered record start sequence and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE (parg->tisn and parg->mst have already been changed); on success it sets expected_seq to the packet sequence and returns MLX5E_TLS_LOOP. In the in-order case it counts statistics, advances expected_seq by the payload length, sets parg->tisn, parg->ihs and parg->mst and returns MLX5E_TLS_CONTINUE.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: parg->tisn and parg->mst are set before mlx5e_sq_dump_xmit (mlx5_en_hw_tls.c:854-855) and remain changed on the FAILURE return at 858-861; the old text said parg is untouched. Original reviewer right that the no-tag and non-TLS CONTINUE returns change nothing. Real function at 763-876 (slice 763-893). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: update_buffer_lossy
prose: Precondition: priv, buffer (an array of MLX5E_MAX_PRIORITY priority-to-buffer entries), port_buffer and change are valid. For each of MLX5E_MAX_BUFFER buffers it counts the priorities mapped to it and how many of them have their bit clear in pfc_en, and sets the lossy flag to 1 if all mapped priorities are non-PFC (a buffer with no priorities mapped also gets lossy = 1), else 0, updating port_buffer->buffer[i].lossy and noting whether any flag changed. If none changed it returns 0 and leaves *change unmodified. If at least one changed it calls update_xoff_threshold(priv, port_buffer, xoff): a nonzero result is returned with *change not set (the lossy flags in port_buffer have already been modified); otherwise it sets *change to true and returns 0. The mtu argument is not used.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: mtu is never used in the body (mlx5_en_port_buffer.c:192-237). Original reviewer right that *change stays unmodified on an update_xoff_threshold error (229-233). Read in full.

name: mlx5e_port_manual_buffer_config
prose: Precondition: priv is a valid mlx5e_priv; change is a bit mask of MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_* flags; pfc must be non-NULL when MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_PFC is set, buffer_size must point to MLX5E_MAX_BUFFER entries when MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_SIZE is set, and prio2buffer to MLX5E_MAX_PRIORITY entries when MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_PRIO2BUFFER is set. It computes xoff with calculate_xoff, queries the current port buffer (returning the error), and per flag: CABLE_LEN marks an update and recomputes the xoff thresholds; PFC queries the priority-to-buffer map, sets priv->sw_is_port_buf_owner to true and calls update_buffer_lossy with pfc->pfc_en; PRIO2BUFFER marks a priority-map update, queries the current PFC enable and calls update_buffer_lossy with the new map; SIZE sets each buffer size from buffer_size, returning -EINVAL if a non-lossy buffer has size 0 or if the total exceeds port_buffer.port_buffer_size, marks an update and recomputes the thresholds. Each failing step returns its error at once (earlier steps may already have changed port_buffer in memory and sw_is_port_buf_owner). If no buffer update is pending and xoff differs from priv->dcbx.xoff it recomputes the thresholds and marks an update. It then stores xoff into priv->dcbx.xoff (before any hardware write), and if an update is pending sets sw_is_port_buf_owner to true and calls port_set_buffer (returning its error, with dcbx.xoff already updated), then, if a priority-map update is pending, sets sw_is_port_buf_owner to true and returns the result of mlx5e_port_set_priority2buffer; otherwise it returns err, which is 0 at that point.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: priv->dcbx.xoff is assigned at mlx5_en_port_buffer.c:323 before port_set_buffer and mlx5e_port_set_priority2buffer, so those failures leave it updated; the old text said it was unchanged. Real function at 239-339 (slice 255-339 cut the head). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: mlx5e_rl_sysctl_handler
prose: Precondition: arg1 is the mlx5e_rl_priv_data (with a valid priv) and arg2 indexes rl->param.arg. It takes PRIV_LOCK(priv) for its whole body (released at the done label on every path) and reads the stored value under the RL read lock. If req is non-NULL it calls sysctl_handle_64 and returns without changes (with that error, or 0) if the call failed, req->newptr is NULL, or the value equals the stored one; if req is NULL it does not return early: the stored value is used and it continues. It then returns ENXIO if priv->gone is set. Otherwise it records whether the rate-limit workers are open and whether cq_period_mode_modify is supported, and by parameter: tx_worker_threads_def, tx_channels_per_worker_def and tx_rates_def are clamped to [1, their max] and stored; tx_coalesce_usecs and tx_coalesce_pkts are clamped to [0, field max] (values below 1 become 0), stored, and if the workers are open the error of mlx5e_rl_refresh_channel_params is returned; tx_coalesce_mode is normalised to 0 or 1 and stored, and if the workers are open it either closes and reopens them (when mode modification is unsupported) or returns the refresh error (when supported); tx_queue_size is clamped to [1 << MLX5E_PARAMS_MINIMUM_LOG_SQ_SIZE, tx_queue_size_max], rounded to a power of two, stored with the workers closed and reopened if they were open, and the completion factor resynced; tx_completion_fact is stored the same way; tx_limit_add and tx_limit_clr return the error from mlx5e_rl_tx_limit_add / mlx5e_rl_tx_limit_clr; tx_allowed_deviation and tx_burst_size are clamped to their min and max and stored under the RL write lock; any other index changes nothing. The error variable is returned (0 except where a branch set it).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: req == NULL does not return early (mlx5_en_rl.c:1457-1464) and the code goes on to the gone check and parameter switch. Round 2 reviewer right that tx_coalesce_mode depends on cq_period_mode_modify (1535-1554), included now. Original reviewer right that the channel-parameter refresh happens only for the coalesce parameters. Real function at 1441-1635 (slice 1279-1529). Read in full; the exact set of error values from tx_limit_add and tx_limit_clr was not verified.

name: mlx5e_rl_worker
prose: Precondition: arg is an initialised mlx5e_rl_worker (mutex, condvar, priv, channels, process_head and index_list_head valid) and the thread holds neither the worker lock nor the rate lock. It raises the thread priority, takes the worker lock, then for each of tx_channels_per_worker_def channels (skipping FREE channels unless HAVE_RL_PRE_ALLOCATE_CHANNELS is defined) it drops the worker lock, opens a send queue with mlx5e_rl_open_channel under the RL read lock, re-takes the worker lock, stops the loop after logging at the first failure, and otherwise sets the channel's rate to init_rate (the result of that rate setting is ignored). It then loops: it waits on the condvar while the process queue is empty and leaves the loop when worker_done is nonzero; it takes the first queued channel: for state MODIFY it sets the state to USED, then opens an SQ (logging an error, or incrementing tx_open_queues on success) if the channel has none, else resumes its SQ, and then sets the rate to new_rate * 8 (an error is logged); for state DESTROY it sets the rate to 0 (an error is logged), drains the SQ if there is one, inserts the channel at the head of index_list_head, sets the state to FREE and decrements tx_active_connections; other states are ignored. After the loop it goes through all tx_channels_per_worker_def channels: it copies last_rate to init_rate, sets the rate to 0 (result ignored), and closes the SQ (with the lock dropped) and decrements tx_open_queues if the channel has an SQ; the channel state is not changed. Finally it clears worker_done, broadcasts the condvar, releases the worker lock and calls kthread_exit.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the rate-setting results in the initial loop and in the final loop are not checked (mlx5_en_rl.c:640, 726); only the MODIFY and DESTROY branches log them. Original reviewer right that the final loop does not set channel->state to FREE. Real function at 592-741 (slice 509-763). Read in full; the callee functions were not read.

name: syndrome_to_errno
prose: Precondition: none; syndrome is an enum mlx5_ipsec_response_syndrome value and any integer is accepted. It returns 0 for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_SUCCESS (value 0), -EINVAL for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_ILLEGAL_REQUEST (value 1), -EEXIST for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_SADB_ISSUE (value 2), -EIO for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_WRITE_RESPONSE_ISSUE (value 3), and -EIO for every other value. It has no side effects.
note: Checked against the enum values at mlx5fpga_ipsec.c:43-46 and the switch at 111-124 (read in full): 1 maps to -EINVAL and 2 to -EEXIST, as the old prose said. Reviewer reasons were only mechanical. Contract left empty because the return values are negative errno macros.

name: mlx5_fpga_device_reload
prose: Precondition: fdev is an initialised mlx5_fpga_device with a valid mdev. It reads fdev->fdev_state under state_lock: MLX5_FDEV_STATE_NONE gives -ENODEV and IN_PROGRESS gives -EBUSY (returned without taking the interface mutex). Otherwise it takes mdev->intf_state_mutex and holds it until return. For image MLX5_FPGA_IMAGE_RELOAD it returns the result of mlx5_fpga_device_reload_cmd without unregistering the device or changing MLX5_INTERFACE_STATE_UP. For any other image it clears MLX5_INTERFACE_STATE_UP, unregisters and stops the device, sets fdev_state to IN_PROGRESS and re-initialises load_event; then for image <= MLX5_FPGA_IMAGE_FACTORY it calls mlx5_fpga_load, for MLX5_FPGA_IMAGE_RESET it issues the reset control operation (a failure of either returns that error), and for any other image it logs an unknown command and returns err, which is 0 at that point. After a load or reset it calls wait_for_completion_timeout on load_event; if the value assigned to err is negative it sets fdev_state to MLX5_FDEV_STATE_FAILURE and returns it (a timeout, which returns 0, is not treated as an error). It then calls mlx5_fpga_device_start (a nonzero result is returned) and mlx5_register_device; if registration fails it sets fdev_state to FAILURE, stops the fpga device and returns the error; otherwise it sets MLX5_INTERFACE_STATE_UP and returns 0. In none of the paths is fdev_state set to MLX5_FDEV_STATE_SUCCESS by this function. The mutex is released on all paths after it was taken.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right that the wait result is tested (mlx5fpga_sdk.c:428-433), though the stored value is the unsigned return of wait_for_completion_timeout assigned to an int. Round 2 reviewer right that SUCCESS is not set here and the unknown image returns 0. Round 1 reviewer right that RELOAD does not re-register the device (391-394). Also the register-failure path stops the FPGA device (456-459), which the old text omitted. Real function at 364-463 (slice 255-512). Read in full; callees not read.

name: mlx5_ib_poll_cq
prose: Precondition: ibcq is a valid completion queue, num_entries is nonnegative and wc has room for num_entries completions. It takes cq->lock with interrupts saved and releases it on every path. If the core device state is MLX5_DEVICE_STATE_INTERNAL_ERROR it calls mlx5_ib_poll_sw_comp (software completions from the attached QPs) and returns the number it reports, without touching cq->wc_list and without polling hardware. Otherwise, if cq->wc_list is non-empty it polls soft completions with poll_soft_wc (count soft_polled), then calls mlx5_poll_one for up to num_entries - soft_polled entries, stopping at the first call that returns nonzero; each call that returns 0 increments npolled; if npolled is nonzero it updates the CQ consumer index with mlx5_cq_set_ci. It returns soft_polled + npolled, which is at most num_entries as far as the loop bounds show.
note: Round 1 reviewer right: the internal-error path polls QP software completions, not cq->wc_list (mlx5_ib_cq.c:679-681). Round 15 reviewer's claim (the count may include a resize CQE that produces no completion) was not verified because mlx5_poll_one was not read; the prose counts exactly the calls to mlx5_poll_one that returned 0 (687-690). Function at 668-698 (slice 507-759). Read in full.

name: mlx5_query_mad_ifc_port
prose: Precondition: ibdev is a valid mlx5_ib device, port a 1-based port number, props a caller-owned writable struct ib_port_attr. It returns -EINVAL (props untouched) if port is below 1 or above the num_ports capability. It allocates an input and an output MAD (-ENOMEM, props untouched, if either allocation fails; both buffers are freed on every return after allocation). It zeroes *props, issues a PortInfo query for the port with mlx5_MAD_IFC and returns that error (with *props left zeroed) if it fails. Otherwise it fills lid, lmc, sm_lid, sm_sl, state, phys_state, port_cap_flags, gid_tbl_len, max_msg_sz, pkey_tbl_len (from mdev->port_caps[port - 1]), the counters, widths, speed, MTU, subnet_timeout, max_vl_num and init_type_reply from the response. If the extended-speeds capability flag is set it replaces active_speed with 16 (extended speed code 1) or 32 (code 2). If active_speed is 4 and the port's extended capability includes MLX_EXT_PORT_CAP_FLAG_EXTENDED_PORT_INFO, it issues a second MAD (extended port info); if that fails it returns the error with *props already filled from the first response; if bit 0 of its data byte 15 is set it sets active_speed to 8. It returns 0 on success.
note: Packet name mlx5_ib_query_port does not exist in this file; the real function is mlx5_query_mad_ifc_port at mlx5_ib_mad.c:493-583 (read in full), so it is fixed under that name. Old prose omitted the -EINVAL and -ENOMEM returns before props is zeroed and the condition active_speed == 4 for the second MAD. Reviewer reasons were only mechanical.

name: reg_umr
prose: Precondition: pd and umem are valid, order is a valid cache order index, and npages, page_shift and the other arguments describe the region. It tries once to take a cached MR with alloc_cached_mr(dev, order); if none is available it calls add_keys for one key (a failure other than -EAGAIN is only logged) and does not retry, so if the cached MR is still NULL it returns ERR_PTR(-EAGAIN). It then maps the page address list with dma_map_mr_pas; on failure it frees the cached MR with free_cached_mr and returns ERR_PTR of that error (umrc->sem has not been taken yet). Otherwise it prepares the UMR work request, takes umrc->sem, posts it with ib_post_send; if the post fails it goes to unmap_dma with err set; otherwise it waits for the completion and sets err to -EFAULT if the completion status is not IB_WC_SUCCESS. After a successful post (whether or not the completion succeeded) it sets mmkey.iova, mmkey.size, mmkey.pd and marks mr->live = 1. At unmap_dma it releases umrc->sem, unmaps the DMA buffer and frees the temporary page list. If err is nonzero it frees the cached MR with free_cached_mr and returns ERR_PTR(err); otherwise it returns the MR.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: umrc->sem is taken only at line 709, after the -EAGAIN and dma_map_mr_pas failure exits, so those exits do not release it (mlx5_ib_mr.c:695-701, 709, 728-737). Original reviewer right that there is no retry after add_keys and that a failed add_keys yields -EAGAIN via the NULL mr (683-696). Detail added: mr->live and the key fields are set even when the completion failed, before the MR is freed (722-737). Real function at 665-741 (slice 506-765). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: mlx5_ib_update_mtt
prose: Precondition: mr is a live MTT-mode MR with a valid umem, and start_page_index and npages describe a range inside it; the caller keeps mr and its umem alive. It first rounds start_page_index down to a multiple of MLX5_UMR_MTT_ALIGNMENT / 8 (growing npages by the difference) and rounds the page count up to that alignment. If the aligned range would exceed MLX5_MAX_UMR_PAGES it returns -EINVAL immediately, before allocating anything. Otherwise it gets a zeroed page with get_zeroed_page(GFP_ATOMIC) as the page buffer; if that fails it falls back to a static emergency buffer of MLX5_UMR_MTT_MIN_CHUNK_SIZE bytes, taking mlx5_ib_update_mtt_emergency_buffer_mutex. It maps the buffer for DMA; if the mapping fails it returns -ENOMEM after freeing the page or releasing the mutex. It then processes the range in chunks that fit the buffer: for each chunk it copies the page addresses for the chunk from the umem into the buffer unless zap is set (with zap the buffer's existing contents, zero, are used), posts a UMR work request to update the MTT under umrc->sem (taken and released per chunk), and waits for its completion. A failed ib_post_send ends the loop with its error; a completion status other than IB_WC_SUCCESS ends it with -EFAULT; chunks before the failing one have been written and later ones not. After the loop it unmaps the DMA buffer. At the exit it frees the page buffer or, if the emergency buffer was used, releases the emergency mutex, and returns 0 or the error.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the -EINVAL return at mlx5_ib_mr.c:775-776 occurs before the allocation and before any DMA mapping, so the statement that every return path tears down the mapping and frees the page or releases the mutex is only true for the paths after allocation. Real function at 744-863 (slice 766-1018 cut the head). Read in full; __mlx5_ib_populate_pas and the UMR completion machinery not read.

name: create_raw_packet_qp
prose: Precondition: dev, qp, in and pd are valid and pd->uobject is non-NULL with a ucontext (it is dereferenced at the start to obtain the user context's transport domain number tdn). If qp->sq.wqe_cnt is nonzero it creates the TIS and then the SQ (a TIS failure returns its error at once; an SQ failure destroys the TIS) and sets sq->base.container_mibqp = qp. If qp->rq.wqe_cnt is nonzero it sets rq->base.container_mibqp = qp, creates the RQ (on failure it destroys the SQ and TIS if the send queue exists) and then the TIR (on failure it destroys the RQ, and then the SQ and TIS if the send queue exists). If everything succeeded it sets qp->trans_qp.base.mqp.qpn to the SQ's qpn when a send queue exists, otherwise the RQ's qpn, and returns 0. On failure it returns the error from the failing create helper after destroying the objects this call created, in reverse order.
note: Round 17 reviewer is wrong: the function does dereference pd->uobject (uobj->context at mlx5_ib_qp.c:1279). name: mlxfw_firmware_flash
prose: Precondition: mlxfw_dev has valid ops (fsm_lock, fsm_state_wait path, fsm_activate, fsm_release) and firmware points to a readable image. It returns -EINVAL if the image is not an MFA2 file and returns PTR_ERR of mlxfw_mfa2_file_init if the file cannot be parsed (neither case locks anything). Otherwise it calls fsm_lock: if that fails it finalises the MFA2 file with mlxfw_mfa2_file_fini and returns the error without calling fsm_release. After a successful lock it waits for the LOCKED state, flashes all components, calls fsm_activate and waits for LOCKED again; if any of these steps fails it calls fsm_release, finalises the MFA2 file and returns that error. If all succeed it calls fsm_release, logs completion, finalises the MFA2 file and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: the success path does call fsm_release (mlxfw_fsm.c:250-251). Original reviewer's point (fsm_lock failure skips fsm_release) is right and was already stated (224-228, 262-263). Real function at 207-265 (slice 253-273 only covered the tail). Read in full; mlxfw_flash_components and the state wait helper not read.

name: mmc_switch_status
prose: Precondition: timeout (in microseconds) is nonzero (KASSERTed, effective only in kernels with INVARIANTS). It polls the card status with mmc_send_status, retrying a send that returns MMC_ERR_BADCRC up to 10 times in a row; any other send error, or a BADCRC on the tenth try, ends the loop and is returned. When the status shows the TRAN state the loop ends with err = MMC_ERR_NONE. If the state is not TRAN it computes the deadline (timeout microseconds after the first non-TRAN check) and keeps polling until the current time passes it, then ends the loop with MMC_ERR_TIMEOUT. After the loop, only if err is MMC_ERR_NONE and the last status has R1_SWITCH_ERROR set (which can only be the TRAN-state case), it returns MMC_ERR_FAILED; otherwise it returns err (MMC_ERR_NONE, a send_status error, or MMC_ERR_TIMEOUT). A status with R1_SWITCH_ERROR set but not in the TRAN state does not end the loop and ends in MMC_ERR_TIMEOUT if the card never reaches TRAN.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: SWITCH_ERROR with a non-TRAN state keeps polling and returns MMC_ERR_TIMEOUT (mmc_subr.c:222-234). Original reviewer right that send_status errors can be returned. Real function at 191-237 (slice 1-253). Read in full.

name: mpi3mr_process_op_reply_desc
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid softc, reply_desc is a reply descriptor from an operational reply queue and reply_dma points to writable storage; the descriptor's host tag indexes sc->cmd_list. It sets *reply_dma to 0 and decodes the descriptor by type: a status descriptor supplies the host tag and IOC status (and log info when the status bits are set); an address-reply descriptor supplies the reply frame address in *reply_dma, maps it with mpi3mr_get_reply_virt_addr (if that is NULL it logs and goes to out without touching a ccb) and then takes host tag, IOC status, SCSI status and state, transfer count, sense count and the sense buffer from the reply frame; a success descriptor supplies only the host tag. It takes the command cm from sc->cmd_list[host_tag] and goes to out if its state is MPI3MR_CMD_STATE_FREE. Otherwise, when sc->iot_enable is set, it works on the I/O throttling state: for a command whose block count is at least sc->io_throttle_data_length on a throttle-enabled target it subtracts the block count from sc->pend_large_data_sz and, if the target has a throttle group, from the group's counter, and clears the group's (or, for a target without a group, the target's) io_divert flag (and sets the divert flags of the group's volumes) when the pending counts are at or below the low-water marks; a target that is diverting but does not meet the first condition gets a similar low-water check. A success descriptor sets CAM_REQ_CMP and goes to out_success. For others, a data underrun with zero transferred bytes and a BUSY, RESERVATION_CONFLICT or TASK_SET_FULL SCSI status is treated as IOC success; valid sense data with a nonzero count and a sense buffer is copied into csio (with sense_resid) and CAM_AUTOSNS_VALID is set. The CAM status then depends on the IOC status: BUSY and INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES give CAM_REQUEUE_REQ; SCSI_DEVICE_NOT_THERE gives CAM_REQ_CMP for a volume (targ->devinfo == 0) else CAM_DEV_NOT_THERE; the three terminated codes give CAM_SCSI_BUSY; DATA_OVERRUN sets resid 0 and CAM_DATA_RUN_ERR; DATA_UNDERRUN sets resid to the command length minus the transfer count and, like RECOVERED_ERROR and SUCCESS, with no reply frame gives CAM_REQ_CMP for IOC success or CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR otherwise, and with a reply frame is decided by the SCSI state and status (CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR for no-status or terminated states, CAM_AUTOSENSE_FAIL, CAM_REQ_ABORTED for command-terminated or task-aborted status, CAM_REQ_CMP for GOOD status, else CAM_SCSI_STATUS_ERROR, with sense copied when the sense state is valid); INVALID_SGL gives CAM_UNREC_HBA_ERROR; EEDP, protocol, internal-error and every other IOC status set resid to the command length and CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR. At out_success, if the ccb status is not CAM_REQ_CMP it sets CAM_DEV_QFRZN and freezes the device queue; it decrements the target's outstanding count, completes the command with mpi3mr_cmd_done and decrements sc->fw_outstanding. At out, if a sense buffer was found it reposts it to the controller. The function returns nothing.
note: Packet name mpi3mr_scsi_cmd_completion does not exist; the real function is mpi3mr_process_op_reply_desc at mpi3mr.c:4685-5072 (read in full; logging calls skipped). The old prose stopped at the slice end and said the code 'continues past the end of the provided source'; the part after is now included. Part not checked line by line: the IO-throttle divert block at 4772-4882 was summarised, and whether the first status descriptor/IOC-log fields have further side effects was not examined.

name: mpi3mr_pel_wait_complete
prose: Precondition: drvr_cmd is the completed PEL wait command; if MPI3MR_CMD_REPLYVALID is set in its state, drvr_cmd->reply points to a valid reply. If MPI3MR_CMD_RESET is set it only resets the command (state MPI3MR_CMD_NOTUSED, callback NULL, retry_count 0) and leaves sc->pel_wait_pend unchanged. If no valid reply is present it logs, clears sc->pel_wait_pend and resets the command (no retry). Otherwise, if the IOC status is not success or the PEL log status is neither success nor aborted, it retries: while retry_count is below MPI3MR_PELCMDS_RETRYCOUNT it increments it, calls mpi3mr_issue_pel_wait(sc, drvr_cmd) and returns (the command is not reset by this function; whether the reissue succeeds was not read); after the retries are used up it clears pel_wait_pend and resets the command. If the status is success or aborted it calls mpi3mr_app_send_aen and, unless sc->pel_abort_requested is set, clears sc->pel_cmds.retry_count and calls mpi3mr_send_pel_getseq(sc, &sc->pel_cmds); in this success case drvr_cmd itself is not reset and pel_wait_pend is not cleared by this function.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right that the retry path hands the command to mpi3mr_issue_pel_wait (mpi3mr_app.c:1374-1375) which may itself fail and reset the command; the old text said the command is simply left pending. Original reviewer right that the RESET path does not clear pel_wait_pend (1351-1352, 1393-1396). Read in full at 1343-1397; the issue and send helpers were not read.

name: mpi3mr_pel_getseq_complete
prose: Precondition: drvr_cmd is the completed PEL get-sequence command; if MPI3MR_CMD_REPLYVALID is set its reply points to a valid reply. If MPI3MR_CMD_RESET is set it only resets the command (state NOTUSED, callback NULL, retry_count 0) and leaves sc->pel_wait_pend unchanged. If no valid reply is present it logs, clears sc->pel_wait_pend and resets the command. If the IOC status is not success or the PEL log status is not success it retries: while retry_count is below MPI3MR_PELCMDS_RETRYCOUNT it increments it, calls mpi3mr_send_pel_getseq(sc, drvr_cmd) and returns (no reset is done by this function; the outcome of the resend was not read); after the retries it clears pel_wait_pend and resets the command. On success it sets sc->newest_seqnum to the little-endian Newest value from sc->pel_seq_number plus one, clears retry_count and calls mpi3mr_issue_pel_wait(sc, drvr_cmd).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right that the retry path calls mpi3mr_send_pel_getseq (mpi3mr_app.c:1510-1511), which may itself fail, so the command is not simply left pending. Original reviewer right that a RESET leaves pel_wait_pend alone. Read in full at 1479-1528; helper functions not read.

name: mpi3mr_app_construct_sgl
prose: Precondition: sc has an ioctl chain SGE buffer; mpi_request is a writable request frame (MPI3MR_AREQ_FRAME_SZ bytes when is_rmc is 0, or a management passthrough request when is_rmc is nonzero); dma_buffers has bufcnt entries; num_datasges is the number of data SGEs to build. It first computes the total number of SGEs needed. For is_rmc it writes the CommandSGL pointing at the first buffer, sets the SGL position inside that buffer after user_buf_len, and returns -1 if the needed SGEs exceed the room in it; it then marks the chain as already in use (so no chain SGE is ever created for this case), writes the ResponseSGL from the next buffer when is_rmr is set or a zero-length ResponseSGL otherwise, and builds the data SGEs if num_datasges is nonzero. For is_rmc zero it returns -1 if sgl_offset is not below MPI3MR_AREQ_FRAME_SZ or no SGE slot fits. If num_datasges is 0 it writes a zero-length SGE and returns 0. For an SMP passthrough function it returns -1 if more than 2 SGEs are needed or more than are available, else writes one last-flagged simple SGE per non-skipped buffer and returns 0. Otherwise it builds simple SGEs from each buffer's descriptors (skipping buffers whose data direction is MPI3MR_APP_DDN and writing a zero-length SGE for buffers without descriptors), with end-of-buffer on each buffer's last SGE and end-of-list on the very last. When the initial frame is down to one free slot and more than one SGE is still needed it switches to a chain: it returns -1 if the chain buffer is too small, writes a last-chain SGE pointing at sc->ioctl_chain_sge, zeroes the chain buffer and continues there. When the chain (or, for is_rmc, the management buffer) runs out of slots it returns -1. It returns 0 on success. On a -1 return the SGEs already written (the command and response SGLs, any chain SGE and the zeroed chain buffer) stay as written. No locks are taken.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: for is_rmc the code sets chain_used and returns -1 when the SGEs exceed the management buffer (mpi3mr_app.c:651-653, 720-721), so there is no chain fallback for that case. Round 2 reviewer right about the SMP -1 return when more than two SGEs are needed (684-685). Round 1 right that partial writes remain after a failure. Real function at 620-755 (slice 524-802). Read in full; mpi3mr_add_sg_single and the SGE-count helper not read.

name: mpi3mr_app_mptcmds
prose: Precondition: uarg points to a kernel copy of a struct mpi3mr_ioctl_mptcmd whose user pointers (mpi_msg_buf, buf_entry_list, and each buffer entry's user buffer) are user addresses; dev, cmd, flag and td are unused in what was read; the caller may sleep. The initial return value is EINVAL. It returns ENODEV if no adapter matches karg->mrioc_id, ENOMEM if the ioctl SGE DMA memory was not allocated, raises karg->timeout to at least MPI3MR_IOCTL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, returns EINVAL (nothing allocated) if mpi_msg_size or buf_entry_list_size is zero or mpi_msg_size * 4 exceeds MPI3MR_AREQ_FRAME_SZ, and returns ENOMEM if the request frame allocation fails. After that all failures go to the out label, which frees kern_erb, the buffer list, the MPI request frame, the per-buffer DMA descriptors and the dma_buffers array and the reply buffer when allocated, and returns the code. It copies in the MPI request (EFAULT on failure) and the buffer entry list (ENOMEM if its allocation fails, EFAULT on copyin failure), validates the entries and sets up the kernel and DMA buffers (EINVAL for an empty or invalid entry list or invalid sizes, ENOMEM for allocation failures, EFAULT for copyin failures; the exact checks in this stretch, lines 836-1004, were only checked by their return statements). It then returns EAGAIN if an ioctl command is already pending, if a reset is in progress or if ioctls are blocked, and EFAULT if the controller is in an unrecoverable state. For non-NVMe functions it builds the SGL with mpi3mr_app_construct_sgl (EAGAIN on failure); the NVMe-encapsulated branch has its own checks returning ENOMEM or EINVAL. For a SCSI task-management request other than abort-task it looks up the target by device handle (ENODEV if not found) and increments its block_io count. It marks the ioctl command pending, posts it with mpi3mr_submit_admin_cmd (a nonzero result is returned after the out_failed cleanup) and waits for completion with the timeout; on a timeout it returns EAGAIN and, unless the command was already reset, requests a soft reset. On completion it copies the MPI reply, the sense data and the data-in buffers back to user space (ENOMEM if a reply buffer cannot be allocated, EFAULT on copyout failure), and returns 0. out_failed also decrements the target's block_io count if one was taken and clears the ioctl command state before falling to out.
note: Packet name unnamed-ioctl-issue-handler is the function mpi3mr_app_mptcmds at mpi3mr_app.c:779-1218 (long return type, returns errno values as positive numbers). Round 17 reviewer is wrong: the SCSI task-management target lookup with ENODEV exists at 1065-1074. Partly read: only the start (800-835), the pending/reset/block checks (1005-1040), the task-management and submit/wait part (1062-1105) and the return, goto and rval lines of the whole function were read; the buffer-entry parsing (836-1004), the NVMe branch (1040-1062) and the copy-back loops (1106-1193) were not read line by line, so details there are only as listed by their return/goto lines.

name: mpr_user_pass_thru
prose: Precondition: sc is an initialised mpr_softc whose lock the caller does not hold, and data is a kernel copy of an mpr_pass_thru_t whose pointers are user addresses. It takes the softc lock; if MPR_FLAGS_BUSY is already set it releases the lock and returns EBUSY with nothing else touched; otherwise it sets MPR_FLAGS_BUSY and releases the lock. It checks the direction: valid combinations are DataSize 0 with direction NONE, or a nonzero DataSize with READ, WRITE, or BOTH with a nonzero DataOutSize; for a valid BOTH request the direction is rewritten to READ, for other valid ones DataOutSize is set to 0; an invalid combination returns EINVAL. It returns EINVAL if RequestSize exceeds sc->reqframesz, copies the request in (returning the copyin error). For a SCSI task-management request it allocates a TM command (EINVAL if none), finds the target by DevHandle, and if the target is unknown or mpr_wait_command fails sets EIO; with a reply it copies up to MIN(reply size, ReplySize) bytes of the reply to the user and returns the copyout result; the TM command is freed. For other requests it allocates a command (ENOMEM if none), copies in the request, sets up the data buffer, copying in the data-out (or write) data (a copyin failure goes to the cleanup), checks the SCSI I/O handle fields (EINVAL cases at lines 1007 and 1035) and waits for completion with mpr_wait_command (30 s); on an error or a NULL command it returns the error. On completion it syncs and unloads the DMA map, copies data-in to the user, copies the reply (up to MIN of the reply size and ReplySize), copies SCSI sense data for SCSI I/O functions when autosense is valid, and copies the NVMe error response for NVMe-encapsulated functions, where a NULL error response buffer only logs and the function proceeds to the cleanup with the err value it had. At the end it clears MPR_FLAGS_BUSY with the lock held, frees the command (and its data buffer if any) and the request copy, releases the lock and returns err (the first copyout error, the wait error, or 0).
note: Packet name mpr_user_passthru does not exist; the real function is mpr_user_pass_thru at mpr_user.c:734-1169. Round 17 reviewer is wrong: the code rewrites BOTH to READ for a valid BOTH request (778-779). Partly read: lines 734-870, 1041-1169 and the returns/gotos/err lines of 870-1040 were read; the SGE and buffer setup between 880 and 1040 (including the SCSI I/O DevHandle EINVAL checks at 1007 and 1035) were not read line by line.

name: mps_read_config_page
prose: Precondition: sc and params are valid and params->hdr describes the page; the caller holds the softc lock as the mps code requires (not checked here). It returns EBUSY without touching params if MPS_FLAGS_BUSY is set or mps_alloc_command returns NULL. Otherwise it builds a CONFIG request (action, page address, and the standard or extended header fields from params->hdr), sets cm_data and cm_length from params->buffer and params->length (with a data-in simple SGE when the buffer is non-NULL) and records params in cm_complete_data. If params->callback is non-NULL it sets mps_config_complete as the completion routine and returns the result of mps_map_command (0, EINPROGRESS or an error); params->status and the header are filled in later by mps_config_complete, and the page data is written into params->buffer by the hardware through DMA. If params->callback is NULL it calls mps_wait_command with no timeout and CAN_SLEEP: on a nonzero error it logs, frees the command if cm is still non-NULL, and returns that error; on success it calls mps_config_complete directly and returns 0. mps_config_complete syncs and unloads the buffer DMA map, sets params->status to MPI2_IOCSTATUS_BUSY if the command had error flags or no reply, else to the reply IOCStatus and copies the reply page header into params->hdr; it frees the command and calls params->callback if non-NULL.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: mps_config_complete only DMA-syncs and unloads params->buffer; the page data is not copied by it (mps.c:3232-3236). Original reviewer right that in the async case params->status and the data are not set when the function returns (3199-3201). Round 2 reviewer's EWOULDBLOCK point was not checked because mps_wait_command was not read; the prose says only 'a nonzero error'. Real function at 3146-3215 (slice 3059-3272), with mps_config_complete at 3223-3272. Read in full.

name: mps_mapping_check_devices
prose: Precondition: data is the mps_softc and sc->mps_mtx is held (asserted); it is the device_check_callout handler. It first sets sc->track_mapping_events to 0. If the callout is pending or not active it returns at once without touching the callout. Otherwise it deactivates the callout and looks at the IOC page 8 mapping mode. In enclosure-slot mapping mode it scans the enclosure table, in device-persistence mapping mode the device mapping table, for an entry with init_complete set; if none is found (or the mode is neither) it re-arms the callout to run again after MPS_MISSING_CHECK_DELAY seconds and returns. Otherwise in enclosure-slot mode, for every enclosure entry not yet init_complete it increments missing_count (if below MPS_MAX_MISSING_COUNT, committing the entry with _mapping_commit_enc_entry when its dpm_entry_num is valid) and sets init_complete; it then returns if the firmware is not IR firmware, else it takes the IR map range of the mapping table. In persistence mode it uses the whole mapping table. It returns if the end index is 0. Over the selected mapping-table range, an entry with MPS_DEV_RESERVED set and physical_id 0 only gets init_complete set; an entry with MPS_DEV_RESERVED set and a nonzero physical_id that is not init_complete gets missing_count incremented (if below the cap, committed with _mapping_commit_map_entry when its dpm_entry_num is valid) and init_complete set; entries without MPS_DEV_RESERVED are left unchanged. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the mapping-table pass touches only reserved entries (mps_mapping.c:2056-2078), not every unprocessed entry. Original reviewer right that reserved entries with zero physical_id only get init_complete (2057-2059) and that the early return skips the table pass (2038-2039, 2054-2055). Real function at 1935-2079 (slice 1808-2080). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: mps_mapping_enclosure_dev_status_change_event
prose: Precondition: sc and event_data are valid objects. The function returns nothing and has an exit label that always flushes pending DPM pages with _mapping_flush_dpm_pages and decrements sc->pending_map_events if it is nonzero. If the IOC page 8 mapping mode is not enclosure-slot mapping it goes straight to that exit. For an MPI2_EVENT_SAS_ENCL_RC_ADDED event: zero reported slots goes to the exit; it looks the enclosure up by logical ID and phy bits; if an entry exists and is init_complete with missing_count 0 it goes to the exit; otherwise it updates the existing entry's handle and start slot, ORs in the phy bits and, if the missing count was nonzero or the phy bits changed, clears missing_count and (when DPM is enabled and the entry has a DPM slot and that DPM entry has a missing count or the phy bits changed) rewrites the DPM entry and marks it for flushing. If no entry exists it takes the next free table index, or, if the table is full, evicts the entry with the highest missing count (adding its DPM entry to the removal table and clearing it); only when no entry can be evicted does it log that the table is full and go to the exit. A new entry is filled from the event (handle, logical ID, slots, start slot, phy bits, BAD indexes for start_index and dpm_entry_num). For both existing and new entries it then sets init_complete. For an MPI2_EVENT_SAS_ENCL_RC_NOT_RESPONDING event it finds the entry by handle (logging and going to the exit if none), increments missing_count up to MPS_MAX_MISSING_COUNT, rewrites its DPM entry with the slot count and missing count when DPM is enabled and the entry has a DPM slot, marks it for flushing and sets init_complete. Other reason codes change nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: a full enclosure table does not always return early; it first tries to evict an entry with a missing count and only exits when none can be evicted (mps_mapping.c:2362-2379). Original reviewer right that the 'mapping mode enabled' precondition was wrong because the function no-ops when the mode is not enclosure-slot mapping, and also for zero slots or an already-present enclosure (2289-2291, 2297-2302, 2319-2325). Real function at 2276-2430 (slice 2081-2381). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: mpssas_ir_shutdown
prose: Precondition: sc is an attached mps softc with initialised mapping_table, sassc and target arrays; the caller does not hold the mps lock (the function takes and releases it around the wait); howto holds the reboot flags. If IR firmware is loaded it computes the volume index range from the IOC page 8 volume mapping mode (starting at 0, or 1 when target ID 0 is reserved, for the low-volume mapping, else at max_devices - max_volumes) and scans the mapping_table indexes from the start up to but not including start + max_volumes - 1 for an entry with a nonzero physical_id and missing_count 0. If such a volume is found it allocates a command (printing a message and skipping the request if that fails), builds a RAID action request with action MPI2_RAID_ACTION_SYSTEM_SHUTDOWN_INITIATED, waits for it with mps_wait_command (5 second timeout, sleeping allowed) under the mps lock, ignores the reply, and frees the command if it is still held. Whether or not any of this happened, it then walks all max_devices targets: for each target with a nonzero handle and supports_SSU set it sets stop_at_shutdown according to sc->enable_ssu: MPS_SSU_DISABLE_SSD_DISABLE_HDD gives FALSE; MPS_SSU_DISABLE_SSD_ENABLE_HDD gives TRUE except for SATA SSDs, which get FALSE; MPS_SSU_ENABLE_SSD_ENABLE_HDD gives TRUE; MPS_SSU_ENABLE_SSD_DISABLE_HDD and any other value give TRUE only for SATA SSDs. Finally it calls mpssas_SSU_to_SATA_devices(sc, howto). It returns nothing.
note: Packet name unnamed_shutdown_function is mpssas_ir_shutdown at mps_sas_lsi.c:1249-1356 (read in full). Round 17 reviewer is right that the old text had the last two enable_ssu cases wrong: the ENABLE_SSD_DISABLE_HDD and default case sets stop_at_shutdown TRUE only for SATA SSDs (1344-1351). The scan loop is 'id < end_idx', so the last volume index is not examined (1281). The old claim that stop_at_shutdown is set 'in every case' was too broad: it is set only for targets with a handle and supports_SSU.

name: mps_do_diag_action
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid mps softc, diag_action is a user address, and return_code points to the caller's code. It saves the incoming *return_code and sets *return_code to MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_SUCCESS. By action: REGISTER sets MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER and MPS_DIAG_FAILURE when length is 0, otherwise copies in a whole diag_register structure (sizeof, regardless of length) and returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE if that copyin fails; UNREGISTER, QUERY and RELEASE set INVALID_PARAMETER and failure when length is smaller than their structure, else copy in the structure (MPS_DIAG_FAILURE on copyin failure) and call the corresponding handler, QUERY also copying the result out after a successful handler (copyout failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE); READ_BUFFER copies in the read-buffer structure first (copyin failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE), sets INVALID_PARAMETER and failure if length is less than BytesToRead, otherwise calls mps_diag_read_buffer and on success copies out all but the PtrDataBuffer member (copyout failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE); any other action sets INVALID_PARAMETER and failure. A copyin or copyout failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE immediately with *return_code still MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_SUCCESS. At the end, if the status is failure, the incoming *return_code was MPS_FW_DIAG_NEW and the new *return_code is not MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_SUCCESS, the status is changed to MPS_DIAG_SUCCESS. It returns the status.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the REGISTER copyin reads sizeof(diag_register) bytes whatever length is, as long as length is nonzero (mps_user.c:1785-1793), so 'at least length bytes' as the buffer contract was insufficient. Original reviewer right that copy failures leave *return_code at SUCCESS. Real function at 1768-1877 (slice 1563-1828). Read in full; the diag handlers were not read.

name: mps_user_pass_thru
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid mps softc whose lock the caller does not hold, and data is a kernel copy of an mps_pass_thru_t with user pointers. It takes the lock; if MPS_FLAGS_BUSY is already set it releases the lock and returns EBUSY, leaving the flag alone; otherwise it sets MPS_FLAGS_BUSY and releases the lock. It returns EINVAL (after the common cleanup) for an invalid DataSize/DataDirection/DataOutSize combination, or if RequestSize exceeds sc->reqframesz; it copies the request from user space and returns the copyin error. For a task-management request it takes the lock, allocates a TM command (EINVAL if none), looks up the target by DevHandle (an unknown target or a failed mps_wait_command both end as EIO), copies the reply to the user when there is one (up to MIN of the reply size and ReplySize; the result of the copyout becomes the return value) and frees the TM command. For other requests it allocates a command (ENOMEM if none), sets up the request and data buffer, and copies in the data-out (or write) data: the result of that copyin is stored in err but no check or jump follows in the lines read, so it can be overwritten by later steps. For SCSI I/O requests with DevHandle 0 it returns EINVAL. It then waits for completion with mps_wait_command (30 s) and, on an error or a NULL command, goes to cleanup with that error. After a successful wait it copies data-in to the user, the reply (up to MIN of reply size and ReplySize) and, for SCSI I/O, the autosense data, each copyout result replacing err. At the end it clears MPS_FLAGS_BUSY with the lock held, frees the command and its data buffer if any and the request copy, releases the lock and returns err. On every path except the initial EBUSY the busy flag is cleared and the request buffer freed.
